question: Can original R11 source-public selected-action consequence counts be used to select an action for an EXPLICIT public intent rather than only predict, without hardcoding desired action names?
inputs: Original R10 exact public image/direction/mission and original R11 learned counts from actually selected and returned source-free public action effects. No environment grid/global pose/carrying private state/door simulator truth.
decision: For each of 7 legal actions, use entire learned empirical outcome distribution and expected declared public intent utility minus nonnegative per-action cost. Do not use preconfigured action-to-key or door mapping. No known positive expected value means abstain. Unknown-context actions cannot be treated as positives. Exact ties lower action ID. Explicitly no autonomous mission parser or map navigation.
training: Source-free manually authored public 7x7x3 observations and selected action/return fixture rows, including no-key and carrying-key otherwise identical door contexts, key pickup, contradictory evidence for one action and a source-free earned public reward example. No actual original Farama MiniGrid episodes.
controls: Independent equally FIT-trained count-table expected-utility conventional controller sees identical public actions/outcomes, source reward, declared utilities/cost, and confidence. Untrained no-evidence abstain control.
metrics: actual chosen legal actions and abstentions in public-context fixtures
exact original R7-R11 source SHA and hosted Linux/Windows source-only tests
vetoes: Source-only functional action selection is not autonomous key retrieval, goal-directed DoorKey navigation or original externally qualified physics
Identical conventional decision across same public training rows prevents native intelligence novelty claim
Source-first frozen evidence must be preserved, and no protected seed or FSA first-use is touched
